references.text: The Israelites also complained in the Desert of Sin and longed for the meat pots of Egypt, showing the same pattern of dissatisfaction with God's provision.
A description of how manna was first given to Israel, which is now all they have to look at.
A description of the manna that Israel now expresses dissatisfaction with.
The immediate context where the people express their longing for the food they had in Egypt.
Later, the people complain again about the manna and call it 'wretched food,' showing persistent dissatisfaction.
The psalm describes how God gave them manna, 'bread from angels,' as a reminder of God's provision.
A reference to Israel's craving in the wilderness and how they put God to the test.
Jesus refers to the manna in the wilderness and contrasts it with the true bread from heaven.
Jesus mentions that their ancestors ate manna in the wilderness and yet died.
Paul refers to the fact that all ate the same spiritual food (the manna) in the wilderness.
